Module 6
Block Storage
Persistent, low-latency storage kept in fixed-size blocks. Other storage types can be scattered across a datacenter while Block Storage works more similarly to a dedicated hard drive

EC2 Instance Store

Temp block-level storage for EC2 Instances
Used for things like buffers, caches, and scratch data.


Elastic Block Store (EBS)

Persistent block-level storage for EC2 instances
Elastic Block Storage Data Lifecycle



EBS Lifecycle

EBS Snapshopts

There is an initial snapshot made on creation
After, there are incremental snapshots of only the changed blocks.




Object Storage
Objects are fundamental units of data storage. Objects typically include data, metadata, and a unique identifier called a key. Objects can be basically anything you think of of whatever size you need.

Objects also have properties like version IDs, access control information, and user-defined metadata.
Buckets are the container used for storing objects in amazon S3
On bucket creation, you specify the name and region
Has settings to configure like versioning, logging, and access permissions

Amazon S3 Storage Classes

S3 Standard

Default option
General-purpose storage for cloud ap
plications, websites, content distribution, mobile/gaming applications, and big-data analytics


S3 Intelligent-Tiering

Automatic tiering based on access patterns.
Three tiers: Frequent, Infrequent, and archive instant access.
Great for data with unknown/changing access patterns.


S3 Standard Infrequent Access / Standard-IA

Self explanatory; Rapid access to infrequently used data
Available in 3 AZs
Great for long-term backups/disaster recovery


S3 One Zone Infrequent Access / One Zone-IA

Same as above, but only available in a single AZ
Reduced availability
Great for data you only kinda care about like secondary backups or recreatable data


S3 Express One Zone

Milisecond data access in one zone
Great for latency-sensitive applications


S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval

Rarely accessed data that requires millisecond retrieval
Cost savings up to 68% compared to S3 standard


S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval

Low-cost storage for archived data accessed 1-2 times a year
Retrieval in 1-5 minutes
Bulk retrieval in up to 5-12 hours with no additional cost
Great for backups, disaster recovery, offsite data storage and other rarely accessed data that do not require fast retrieval times.


S3 Glacier Deep Archive

Same as above but has a default retrieval time of 12 hours
Great for long-term, 7-10+ yr, regulatory compliance requirements.


S3 Outposts

Physical devices shipped to you to bring object storage on-site
Great for maintaining optimal performance for data that must be in close proximity to other on-premises applications.



S3 Lifecycle Configurations
Define life-cycle configurations for an object or group of objects between two types of actions. Use cases include periodic logs needed only for a month and data that changes in access frequency.

Transaction Actions

When objects should transition to another storage class.


Expiration Actions

When objects expire and should be permanently deleted.



File Storage
Amazon Elastic File System (EFS)

NFS-based file storage service
Benefits include:
Multi-AZ redundancy; Auto-replicates data across multiple AZs in a region for high availability
Shared access; Supports thousands of concurrent NFS connections
Elastic Storage; Auto grows/shrinks based on usage to save on costs.
Storage Classes:
Can be configured with data lifecycle rules
Standard
One-Zone (Single AZ)
Archive (higher latency)

Amazon FSx
Same thing as EFS, just for other systems that may not support NFS

AWS Storage Gateway
Hybrid cloud storage service to integrate on-premises environments with the AWS cloud storage. There are three gateway types:

S3 File Gateway

Files written to the server are automatically uploaded to Amazon S3 with intelligent caching


Volume Gateway

Virtual storage volumes with local data access
i.e. local iSCSI volumes that can be mounted by your web applications

Cached Colume Mode

Only frequently-accessed data is stored locally while the rest is sent to the cloud


Stored Volume Mode

keeps entire dataset with asynchronous backups to the cloud as EBS snapshots






Tape Gateway

Replace phyiscal tape infrastructure with virtual tapes.

Replicate your critical local workloads to AWS with minimal downtime.

Monitoring
Amazon CloudWatch

Metrics collection across all AWS resources and on-premises
Can set “alarms” that send notifications or make automatic changes to a resource on a trigger event
Dashboards - Customizable home pages
Collects Logs of your AWS resources
Use case: It can be used to monitor and troubleshoot infrastructure.

Tracks user activity and API usage on AWS as well as other cloud providers.

Compliance
aws.amazon.com/compliance/

On-demand, no cost access to AWS security and compliance reports

Auditing for Compliance

AWS Config

Benefits: AWS Config helps evaluate configurations against a desired state, manage resource configuration changes, and simplify troubleshooting and remediation.


AWS Audit Manager

Benefits: Audit Manager saves time with automated evidence collection, streamlines collaboration across teams, and helps ensure integrity of audits with read-only permissions.

Dashboard
Account Factory
Controls
Landing Zone

It’s the enterprise-wide container that holds OUs, accounts, users, and resources you want to regulate for compliance.




Use cases: Use AWS Control Tower to quickly deploy applications and provision compliant AWS accounts.

AWS Service Catalog

Use cases: Use it to provision resources across AWS accounts, apply access controls, and accelerate provisioning of continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines.

AWS License Manager

Use cases: Use it to streamline license management and to simplify the Microsoft License Mobility through Software Assurance experience. You can also use it to automate the distribution and activation of software entitlements across AWS accounts for end users.

AWS Organizations

Service Control Policies (SCP)

A policy that lets you place restrictions on AWS services, resources, and individual API actions that users and rules in each account can access.

Can be applied toOUs or individual member accounts




Use cases: It can be used for automating AWS account creation, providing tools and access for your security teams, controlling user access to designated services, and sharing common resources across accounts.

AWS Health Dashboard

Use cases: Use AWS Health Dashboard to view account-specific health information. You can also use it to plan for lifecycle events or troubleshoot an incident.

AWS Trusted Advisors ⇐ Look into this further. Is it an AI or a person or what?

All AWS Support plans include access to dozens of Trusted Advisor checks.
Use cases: It can be used to optimize cost, efficiency, security, improve performance, and track service limits.

IAM Access Analyzer

Use cases: It can be used to set fine-grained permissions, verify who can access what, remediate unused access, and refine and remove broad access.

Three phases of the migration process

Migration Frameworks and Strategies
AWS CAF is a cloud migration framework

Use AWS CAF to migrate technology like legacy infrastructure and applications.
Use AWS CAF to migrate and optimize business processes, operations, and create new business models

Six Perspectives of AWS CAF

Business

Business Roles:

Business managers
Finance managers
Budget owners
Strategy stakeholders




People

People Roles:

Human Resources
Staffing
People Managers




Governance

Governance Roles:

Chief Information Officer (CIO)
Program Managers
Enterprise Architects
Business Analysts
Portfolio Managers




Platform

Platform Roles:

Chief technology officer (CTO)
IT managers
Solutions architects




Security

Security Roles:

Chief information security officer (CISO)
IT security managers
IT security analysts




Operations

Operations Roles:

IT operations managers
IT support managers





Seven Migration Strategies

Relocate ; Change the HOST location TO the cloud
Rehost ; Move APPLICATIONS TO the cloud without changes. “Lift and Shift”
Replatform ; Make cloud optimizations before moving to the cloud
Refactor ; Re-imagining how an application is architected and developed
Repurchase ; Repurchasing licenses to a SaaS model / different product
Retain ; Keep business critical applications in their source environments
Retire ; Removing applications that are no longer needed

Migration Services and Tools
Assess Phase
Migration Evaluator

Use cases: You can use Migration Evaluator to conduct broad-based discovery, take a snapshot of your current on-premises footprint to fine-tune licensing, view server dependencies, and gain visibility into multiple migration scenarios. You can also use it to estimate and reduce your cloud costs.

Mobilize Phase
Application Discovery Service

Use cases: You can use the AWS Application Discovery Service to conduct discovery and inventory, map the connections and dependencies, and generate a migration plan.
Migration Hub
Use cases: You can use Migration Hub for migration assessment and planning and migration completion and collaboration with teams. You can also use it for modernization efforts like fast-tracking application refactoring.

Migrate and Modernize Phase
Application Migration Service

Use cases: You can use the Application Migration Service for on-premises applications running on physical servers or infrastructure, cloud-based applications, or moving between AWS Regions. You can also use it to modernize applications.

Database Migrations
AWS Database Migration Service (DMS)

Use cases: You can use AWS DMS to move to managed databases, remove licensing costs, replicate ongoing changes in your database, and improve integration with data lakes.
AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT)
Use cases: You can use AWS SCT to move from commercial databases to open source databases. You can also use it for migrating large data warehouse workloads and modernizing or updating database schemas in place.

Transferring data to and from the AWS Cloud
Online Data Transfer

AWS DataSync

Use cases: You can use DataSync to migrate your data, archive your cold data, and manage hybrid data workflows.


AWS Transfer Family

Use cases: You can use the Transfer Family to modernize and manage your file transfers, simplify data sharing with your workforce and partners, and integrate transactional business data into a unified data lake.
Fully managed for secure file transfers; SFTP FTPS


AWS Direct Connect

AWS Direct Connect is a service that makes it possible for you to establish a dedicated private connection between your network and virtual private cloud (VPC) in the AWS Cloud.
Offline Data Transfer


Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices

Use cases: You can use Snowball Edge devices for data migration when offline migration is required. They can also be used for edge computing when a secure, rugged device is needed.

Duplo-AWS-Cert/Module-13---Well-Architec.content:
AWS Specialized Services and Solutions
Well-Architected Framework

Operational Excellence

Operations, Monitoring, Automation, and Continuous Improvement
Consider EC2 Auto Scaling to scale with your activity!


Security

Protects systems and data through best practices
Least Privilege, Data Integrity, MFA, IAM, throw the lot of security practices!
Consider Strengthening encryption and IAM policies to make things more locked down.


Reliability

Emphasizes recovery and planning and system adaptability to meet changing demands
Consider Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the systems’ health


Performance Efficiency

Encourage using the right resources for the job and adjusting as needs evolve


Cost Optimization

Controls and reduces cost through smart provisioning and resource management


Sustainability

Promote energy-efficient design and environmentally conscious resource usage



AWS Well-Architected Tool
Assists in assessing and improving cloud workloads based on the above six key pillars.

Offers workload reviews, milestone tracking, and custom lenses for tailored evaluations and improvement plans.

Development Services
AWS CodeBuild

fully managed continuous integration service that compiles source code, runs tests, and produces software packages for deployment.
AWS CodePipeline
fully managed CI/CD service that automates the build, test, and deploy phases of your release process.
AWS X-Ray
a powerful tracing, debugging, and performance analysis tool that helps developers visualize application behavior. With X-Ray, developers can quickly identify performance bottlenecks, troubleshoot issues, and optimize applications for better efficiency and reliability.
AWS AppSync
fully managed GraphQL service. Can create a single GraphQL API that securely access, manipulate, and combine data from multiple sources.
AWS Amplify
Streamline the process of developing, deploying, and managing secure/scalable full-stack applications on AWS

Business Application Services
Amazon Connect

Businesses can use this AI-powered contact center service to efficiently set up and operate a scalable customer service call center.
Amazon Simple Email Service (SES)
Amazon SES is a scalable and cost-effective email service provider that can be integrated into any application for reliable, high-volume email automation.

End-user computing services
Amazon AppStream 2.0

FUlly managed service that streams applications from the cloud directly to any compatible device.
SaaS applications
Converts some desktop applications to SaaS
Amazon WorkSpaces
Fully managed Cloud-based desktop computing service.
Virtual desktop
Amazon WorkSpaces Secure Browser (Formerly Amazon WorkSpaces Web)
WorkSpaces Secure Browser is a fully managed remote enterprise browser.

IoT Services

AWS IoT Core is a managed cloud service used to securely connect physical devices with cloud applications.

Duplo-AWS-Cert/Module-4---Going-Global.content:
Designing highly-available architectures
Deploying to multiple regions and zones can achieve high availability. Creating redundant architectures can further that.

High Availability: The capability of a system to operate continuously without failing.
Agility: The ability to quickly adapt to changing requirements or market conditions
Elasticity: The ability of a system to scale up or down automatically depending on demand.

AWS Regions
Regions are massive server farms in geographic locations. USA has the East and West coast regions.
Considerations

Local government Compliance
User Proximity for low response times
Feature availability - Some regions do not have all AWS features
Pricing

Availability Zones
Distinct server farms within a region. Each has its own power, networking, and connectivity.
Edge Locations
Strategically placed server farms between standard regions that cache data and are aimed at providing better latency to users who do not live in or near standard regions. Standard regions in the USA are East Coast and West Coast. Edge Location is in Georgia.
Infrastructure and Automation
CloudFormation
Define infrastructure as code and create templates that describes what you need in terms of infrastructure. CloudFormation takes these templates and worries about the provisioning and resource configurations.

DNS service that provides a reliable and cost-effective way to route end users to internet applications.
Amazon CloudFront
Data caching service that act as the data equivalent of amazon fulfillment centers.

Global Accelerator is a networking service that helps your applications run faster and more reliably across the globe. Think of it like creating express lanes on the internet highway specifically for your application’s traffic.

Duplo-AWS-Cert/Module-6---Storage.content:
Introduction to storage

Block Storage

Used in EC2 instances like hard drives
EC2 instance store:

High-performance storage for temporary data


Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS):

Typical block storage service not specialized for any one thing
EBS Snapshots:

Incremental snapshots; You have one base snapshot of everything and each snapshot after only saves the changes. No duplicate data.
Data Lifecycle Manager: A scheduler for the snapshots






Object Storage

Stores data as objects in a flat address space.
Amazon simple storage service (S3 Standard):

Scalable object storage service to pull data from anywhere
99.999999999% durability
Each object consists of: The data itself, metadata, and a unique identifier called a key
Block Public Access settings override bucket policies


S3 Intelligent Tiering

For data with unknown/changing access patterns.
Objects are stored in three tiers: Frequent access, Infrequent access, archive instant access


S3 Standard Infrequent Access (Standard-IA)

Data that is accessed infrequently, but requires rapid access when it’s needed.


S3 One Zone Infrequent Access (One Zone-IA)

Cheaper version; Store in one availability zone, therefore less availability


S3 Express One Zone

SUPER fast data access in one availability zone
up to 10x faster and up to 80% lower costs than standard


S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval

Rarely access data at lightning speeds


S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval

access data 1-2 times a year
1-5 minute turnaround time for expedited retrieval
5-12 hours turnaround time for bulk retrievals at no extra cost
Ideal for backup, disaster recovery, offsite data storage


S3 Glacier Deep Archive

12 hour retrieval time
Ideal for long-term data storage (7-10 years), mainly to meet regulatory compliance


S3 Outposts

Brings object storage to on-premises!




File Storage

Amazon Elastic File System:

NFS file system
Automatic Multi-AZ redundancy
Supports multiple concurrent NFS connections
Storage classes:

Standard; Highest cost, Highest availability
One Zone; One AZ
Archive; Cost optimized for data access only a few times a year or less

Totally not windows shares…
FSx for Windows File Server
FSx for NetApp ONTAP
FSx for OpenZFS
FSx for Lustre

On-premises device to access unlimited cloud storage

keep physical drives on-site
Cached volume mode: For your frequently accessed data
Stored volume mode: For your datasets and to asynchronous backup to the cloud as EBS snapshots

Virtual tape data while storing tape. Like VHS tape or somethn’

Elastic Disaster Recovery replicates critical workloads to AWS with minimal downtime. Your servers’ block-level data is continuously replicated to AWS
Continuous block-level replication with frequent backup intervals, providing near-instant recovery of servers at the target AWS Region

Duplo-AWS-Cert/Module-8---AI,-ML,-and-Da.content:
The AWS Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning stack is composed of the following three tiers of solutions:

AI services - pre-built models that are already trained to perform specific functions
ML services - a more customized approach with Amazon SageMaker AI where you build, train, and deploy your own ML models with fully managed infrastructure
ML frameworks and infrastructure - a completely custom approach to building models using purpose-built chips that integrate with popular ML frameworks

Extra Non-Amazon Concepts

Deep Learning

Type of machine learning where models are trained using layers of artificial neurons, mimicking the human brain. Each layer summarizes and hands off information to the next layer until the model is complete


Generative AI

Type of deep learning powered by massive ML models known as foundation models (FMs)

FMs are pre-trained on vast collections of data


Traditional ML are trained on one task, FMs can be adapted to perform multiple tasks

LLMs are a popular example of FMs





AWS AI/ML Solutions
Tier 1: Pre-built AWS AI services
Language Services
Amazon Comprehend

Natural language processing used to extract key insights from documents
Use cases: Content classification, customer sentiment analysis, and compliance monitoring
Amazon Polly
Text-to-AIspeech
Use cases: Virtual assistants, e-learning applications, and accessibility enhancements for visually impaired users
Amazon Transcribe
Speech-to-text
Use Cases: Customer call transcription, automated subtitling, and metadata generation for media content.
Amazon Translate
Google translate, but AI powered
Use cases: Document translation and multi-language application integrations

Computer vision and search services
Amazon Kendra

Uses natural language processing to search for answers within large amounts of enterprise content.
Use cases: Intelligent search, chatbots, and application search integration
Amazon Rekognition
Video analysis to identify objects, people, text, ecenes, and activities within images/videos stored in S3
Use cases: Content moderation, identity verification, media analysis, and home automation experiences
Amazon Textract
Extract typed and handwritten text found in documents, forms, and even tables within documents
Use cases: Financial, healthcare, and government form text extraction for quick processing

Conversational AI and personalization services
Amazon Lex

Add voice and text conversation interfaces to applications.
Use cases: Virtual assistants, natural language search for FAQs, and automated application bots
Amazon Personalize
use historical data to build intelligent applications with personalized recommendations for your customers.
Use cases: Personalized streaming, product, and trending recommendations

Tier 2: ML services
Amazon SageMaker AI

fully managed service for training and deploying ML models without worry of infrastructure
Key benefits: Many tools to use, fully managed infrastructure, and automation for ML workflows

Tier 3: ML frameworks and infrastructure
ML frameworks

An ML framework is a software library or tool that provides frameworks for building ML models
AWS ML infrastructure
AWS ML infrastructure, such as ML-optimized Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instances, Amazon EMR, and Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS), can support these custom solutions.

AWS GenAI Solutions
Amazon SageMaker JumpStart

A machine learning hub within SageMaker AI that speeds up the building, training, and deploying of ML models.
Offers a library of pre-built ML solutions such as: Computer vision, NLP, tabular data.
Common uses: Rapid ML deployment, custom fine-tuned solutions, Compare performance for different models before committing
Amazon Bedrock
Fully managed service designed for working with large foundation models and building GenAI apps.
Use Cases:

Enterprise-grade GenAI; Build GenAI apps with high security, privacy, and scalability
Multimodal content generation; Generate multiple content types
Advanced Conversational AI
Uses a single API for interaction
Amazon Q Product Suite


Amazon Q Business

This answer questions, solves problems, and takes actions using enterprise data and expertise
Use cases: Information requests, automated workflows, and insight extraction


Amazon Q Developer

Code recommendations to accelerate development

C#, Jave, JavaScript, Python, and TypeScript
Integrates with multiple IDEs


Use cases: Faster code generation, improved reliability and security, and automated code reviews



Data Analytics
Key Concepts

Data Pipelines for ETL Processes

AI/ML and traditional data analytics requires clean and accessible data that is usable by analytics tools and AIs. Learn the ETL process for data storage:

Extract the data from various sources and store it.
Transform it into a consistent, usable format for downstream tools to consume
Load it into a destination system, like a data warehouse or analytics platform.




Data analytics

Use raw historical data to uncover valuable insights and trends.
Use cases include:

loan companies explaining lending decisions to customers
Medical researchers analyzing clinical trial data through hypothesis testing.
Insurance companies making their risk assessment models transparent for regulators





Data Pipelines
Data Ingestion Services
Data ingestion involves moving data from source systems into your chosen storage solution. Use real-time ingestion when the data is needed immediately. Use batch ingestion when some latency is tolerable.
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams

A serverless service that provides real-time ingestion of terabytes of data applications, streams, and sensors.
On-Demand Mode: Automatic provisioning and scaling
Amazon Data Firehose
Fully managed service for data injection in near real-time.
Used to deliver data within seconds to data lakes, warehouses, and analytics services.

Data Storage Services
Data can come from many different sources. To gain insights, data is commonly consolidated into a single location. There are two storage options for this. Flexible data lakes store vast amounts of raw data. Alternatively, the more structured data warehouses are optimized for business intelligence
Amazon S3

Can be used for data lakes.
Amazon Redshift
Fully managed data warehouse service that can store petabytes of structured or semistructured data.

Data Cataloging Services
Cataloging your data with metadata provides an inventory of your organization’s data.
AWS Glue Data Catalog

Centralized, scalable, and managed metadata repository that enhanced data discovery
Improves efficiency of data pipelines by delivering metadata to various data stores and analytics services.

Data Processing Services
Data processing services clean and transform your data so it’s ready to be analyzed.
AWS Glue

Fully managed ETL service that makes data prep simpler, faster, and cost-effective

Ideal for large-scale data processing and orgs with existing big data enterprise
Auto scales with Infrastructure provisioning, cluster management, and scaling.
Supports Apache Spark, Apache Hadoop, and Apache Hive

Data Analysis and Visualization Services
Queries and visualization tools help you to develop important insights about your data.

run SQL queries to analyze data in relational, nonrelational, object, and custom data sources.
hosted on Amazon S3, on premises, or even in multi-cloud environments.

Fully managed data warehouse solution
Can be used to perform complex SQL queries on large datasets for frequent, high performance analytical workloads
Amazon QuickSight
Quickly create modern interactive dashboards and reports from various data sources without need to manage infrastructure.

Search for relevant content through precise keyword matching or natural language queries.

AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)

Groups such as employees or managers
Individual users
Roles for things like station; Baristas versus cashiers

Centralized identity and access management for use across all AWS accounts and applications.
Can connect to existing identity sources for better SSO access.

Called federated identity management
AWS Secrets Manager


Essentially a password vault that provides a secure way to manage, rotate, and retrieve secrets

ex: Database credentials, API keys, and others.
AWS Systems Manager


Centralized view of nodes across your org’s accounts, regions, multi-cloud, and hybrid environments.
Used to access node information such as ID and operating system details, automate registry edits, user management, and security patching
Nodes are connection points in a network, system, or structure.

Protecting Networks and Applications
AWS Protection Through Services
Protect from DoS and DDoS

Use security groups and elastic load balancing
AWS Shield
Automatically protect AWS customers from the most common types of DDoS attacks at no cost.
AWS Shield Advanced
paid service that provides detailed attack diagnostics and the ability to detect and mitigate sophisticated DDoS attacks.
Integrates with other services like CloudFront, Route 53, ELB
AWS WAF
Web Application Firewall
Monitors network requests that come to web apps.

Checks IP address against a web ACL and blocks when there is a match



Protecting Data
AWS Built-in data protection

S3 has encryption configured by default
EBS volumes and snapshots can be encrypted at rest

Including both boot and data volumes of EC2 instance


DynamoDB

AWS Data Protection Services
AWS Key Management Service (KMS)

Manage yer cryptographic keys
Use the keys across a wide range of services and in your applications

Monitor sensitive data at rest
Uses ML and automation to discover sensitive data stored in Amazon S3.
Meant to assess security posture and to help meet compliance

Centalized manaegment of SSL/TLS certificates

Detecting and Responding to Security Incidents

Runs automated security assessments for EC2 instances, containers, and lambda functions.
Completed assessments can be reviewed in Inspector’s console
Amazon GuardDuty
Threat detection by continuous monitoring streams of account metadata and network activity within the environment.

Section 2: Fundamentals of Security
4. Fundamentals of Security
Security can be about finding the right balance between security and user accessibility

users will find their way around annoying security practices, causing a bigger issue than a less secure option
Must be easy enough for some idiot user to use the fucking thing, but hard enough to prevent malicious activity

Information Security - Act of protecting data and information from unauthorized access, unlawful modification and disruption, disclosure and corruption, and destruction

The data itself, not the device

Information System Security - Act of protecting the systems that hold and process the critical data

The inverse of Information Security

CIA Triad
Confidentiality ensures that information or data is only accessible by authorized users

Only those approved can access a share drive
Integrity ensures that data remains accurate and unaltered unless modification is required
Commonly used documents across multiple LOBs shouldn’t be altered by just anyone and is resilient to data corruption or loss
Availability ensures that data and resources are accessible and functional when needed by authorized users
Websites stay online and up

CIANA Pentagon (CIA Triad ++)
Non-repudiation
Authentication
AAA of Security
Authentication is the process of verifying the identity of a user or system

Credentials, 2FA, etc.
Authorization defines what actions or resources a user can access
Read, Write, Execute permissions
Command/Application permissions
Accounting is the act of tracking user activities and resource usage, typically for audit or bulling purposes
Logs for monitoring for unusual behavior

Security Controls
Measures or mechanisms put in place to mitigate risks and protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information systems and data

Technical
Managerial
Operational
Physical

We do also have more definitions of specific types of security controls

Preventative

Firewall to prevent intrusion


Deterrent

Active monitoring to deter intrusion


Detective

Active monitoring


Corrective

Incident response


Compensating

A management, operational, and/or technical control (i.e., safeguard or countermeasure) employed by an organization in lieu of a recommended security control in the low, moderate, or high baselines that provides equivalent or comparable protection for an information system.


Directive

Policies and procedures that dictate specific actions or behaviors by users or systems
Mandatory password resets



Zero Trust
Zero trust is a security model that operates on the principle that no one, inside or out of the organization, should be trusted by default. In order to implement Zero Trust, we need two planes of operation.

Control Plane consists of the adaptive identity, threat scope reduction, policy-driven access control, and secured zones
Data Plane is focused on the subject/system, policy engine, policy administrator, and establishing policy enforcement points

5. Threats and Vulnerabilities
As cysec professionals cannot control every threat out there, but we can minimize their damage by identifying and fixing vulnerabilities.

Risk management. Find the right balance!
Most vulnerabilities we have power over as they’re typically created by internal factors

Example: Driving to work. Car can break down, might forget it’s “your day” to drive the kids to school, etc.


Most threats are outside of our control ; Outside actors

You can’t control a drunk driver or natural disasters



However you can set protections in place to prevent threats from causing harm.

Example: Leave early for work so that if there is an earthquake or accident, then you will have buffer time to change route

Risk Management is the systematic process of identifying, assessing, and mitigating threats or uncertainties that can affect the organization. It typically involves analyzing the risks’ liklihood and impact, developing strategies to minimizing harm, and monitoring measures’ effectiveness.
OBJ 1.1
13. Security Control Categories
Defense of a castle comes in many
Security control domains:

Technical Controls

Technologies, hardware, and software mechanisms that manage and reduce risks
Antivirus, Firewalls, Encryption processes, Intrusion Detection Systems


Managerial Controls

Involve the strategic planning and governance side of security
Security policies, training programs, and incident response strategies


Operational Controls

Measures that are designed to protect data on a daily basis

Mainly governed by internal processes and human actions


90-day password reset, Backup procedures, account reviews, user training programs


Physical Controls

Real-world measures taken to protect assets ; Physical security
locked doors, fences, gates, cameras, guards, shredding documents



14. Security Control Types

Preventative

proactive measures that prevent harm
Firewall


Deterrent

Measures that deter harm
Warning signs on website


Detective

Monitor and alert malicious activity as they occur or shortly after
IDS


Corrective

Mitigate any potential damage and restore he systems to their normal state



Compensating

Alternative measures for when primary security controls are not feasible or effective



Directive

Standards for behavior within an organization
Company policy



OBJ 1.2
6. Confidentiality
Protecting data from being seen by unauthorized users
important because:

Protect personal privacy
Maintain a business advantage
Achieve regulatory compliance
Regulatory

PII, PHI, various types of financial data



Ensuring Confidentiality:

Encryption

Encryption is Confidentiality


Access Controls ; Setting user access
Data Masking ; Obscuring data
Physical Security
Training and Awareness ; Better training = More confidential employees

7. Integrity
Data should remain accurate and unchanged from their original state unless intentionally modified by an authorized person
important because:

Ensure data accuracy
Maintain Trust
Ensure System Operability

Ensuring Integrity:

Hashing

“Hash Digest”
Hashing is Integrity


Digital Signatures

Create hash digest and then encrypt it with destination’s public key


Checksums

Verify a download’s validity


Access Controls
1.
Regular Audits

8. Availability
Shit should be available when needed by an authorized user
Rule of 9s. Each nine is a period place in 99%. 5 9s is the gold standard
1 9 = 90%
2 9s = 99%
3 9s = 99.9%

8760 hours per year ; Maximum downtime is 8.76 hours

Important because:

Maintaining Customer Trust
Upholding reputation
Loss of revinue
Critical infrastructure like hospitals go down

Ensuring Availability:
REDUNDANCIES

Servers

Using multiple servers in a load balance or switchover in case of failure or overload


Data

RAID, backup systems


Network

If a network path fails, you should have other paths available


Power

Backup power like generators or batteries



9. Non-repudiation
Undeniable proof in digital communications or transactions

Like signing for mail

We use digital signatures to verify these transactions like old kingdom signet rings. Any altering to chains of transactions break the whole thing.

There is practically zero denial of digital signatures. Cant say you didn’t when I have the signature.

Important because:

Confirming the authenticity of digital transactions
Ensuring integrity
Providing accountability

10. Authentication
Ensures individuals or entities are who they claim to be.
Authentication Methods:

Something you know (Knowledge Factor)

Things like a code or password


Something you have (Possession Factor)

Badge, Yubikey, Text passcode


Something you are (Inherence Factor)

Biometric authentication,


Something you do (Action Factor)

Secret handshake, handwriting samples, walking patterns tracked by computers


Somewhere you are (Location Factor)

Relies on the user being in a geographic location for access; Country, building, 20-foot perimeter, etc.



You can combine two or more of these to create a more secure method of authentication. Typically known as MFA or Multi-factor Authentication. Commonly 2FA is how many services run. Send a text and gotta know the password.
11. Authorization
Permissions and privileges granted to users or entities after authentication.
12. Accounting
Security measure that ensures all activities are properly tracked and recorded


Transparency


Security


Accountability


Logging into the system


Accessing Files


Modifying configuration settings


Downloading or installing software


Attempting unauthorized actions on systems and networks


Audit Trail

Chronological record of all user activities



Regulatory Compliance

Maintains a comprehensive record of all users’ activities



Forensic Analysis

Detailed accounting and event logs can help cysec experts



Resource Optimization

Organizations can optimize system performance and minimize costs



User Accountability

Thorough accounting ensures users’ actions are monitored and logged,
Deters potential misuse and promoting adherence to policies.



Syslog servers

Aggregate logs from various network devices



Network Analysis tools

Used to capture and analyze network traffic



SIEMs

Real-time analysis of security alerts



15. Zero Trust
Before, security was conducted like a castle. Strong walls, free access once inside.
Zero trust adds security to inside the castle. Trust nothing and verify everything. Demand verification for every device, user, transaction, regardless of origin.
Zero trust planes:

Control Plane

Overarching framework and set of components responsible for defining, managing, and enforcing policies.


Adaptive Identity

Uses adaptive identities that rely on real-time validation


Threat Scope Reduction

Limit the user’s access to only what they need for work tasks


Policy-driven Access Control

Developing, managing, and enforcing user access based on roles and responsibilities


Secured Zones

Isolated environments on a network that are designed to house data.


Policy Engine

Cross references the access request with its predefined policies


Policy Administrator

Used to establish and manage access policies




Data Plane

Subject/System

Refers to the individual or entity attempting to gain access


Policy Enforcement Point

Allow or restrict access. Acts as a gatekeeper to sensitive areas of the systems or network





16. Gap Analysis
Is the process of evaluating the differences between an organization’s current performance and it’s desired performance
Steps of gap analysis

Define the scope
Gather data on the current state
Analyze the data to identify gaps
Develop a plan to bridge the gap

Types of gap analysis

Technical
Business

Involves evaluating an org’s current business process and identifying where it falls short in fully utilizing cloud-based solutions. Business folk being too stupid to use their tech



Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M)

Addressing specific measures for each vulnerability
Allocate resources and set up timelines for each remediation task ; Set priorities

Section 3: Threat Actors
Threat Actor Motivations

Data Exfiltration
Espionage
Financial Gain
Ethical Reasons

Motivated to improve security ; Also known as Authorized hackers, but it’s more than just that.


Disruption or Chaos

Thrill seeking, challenge their skills, or just plain causing harm ; Also known as unauthorized hackers


Blackmail
Service Disruption
Philosophical or Political Beliefs
Revenge
War

Modern war has modern gadgets and modern supply lines/infrastructure
Both on and off the battlefield



Threat Actor Attributes

Unskilled Attackers
Hacktivists
Organized Crime
Nation-state Actors

Highly Skilled


Insider Threats

Within the organization
Employee revenge
Access Misuse
Shadow IT



Threat Vectors and Attack Surfaces

Messages
Files
Removable Devices
Images
Voice Calls
Usage of unsecured Networks

Outsmarting Threat Actors

Honey…

Pots

Decoy systems/servers


Nets

Decoy network ; Network of honeypots


Files

Decoy Files


Tokens

Decoy user credentials
Can be placed in a DB or system and alerts admins when accessed or used





OBJ 2.1
18. Threat Actor Motivations

All in Section 3 Threat Actors

19. Threat Actor Attributes

Internal vs External

Internal:

Better knowledge of organization and security since there is experience as an employee working with these systems


External:

No authorized access. Must break in




Resources and funding

Lone Hackers < Nation State
Difference between some chud with a ‘top versus russian intelligence officers with unlimited funding


Level of sophistication

Low sophistication

Script kiddies
Me


High sophistication

Researchers
People who can create their own 0-days
Actually smart





20. Unskilled Attackers
An individual who lacks the technical knowledge to develop their own hacking tools or exploits ; Script kiddies with a basic level understanding

Can still cause damage. Just because someone isn’t a gunsmith doesn’t mean they can’t shoot you dead.
Unskilled attackers are less likely to be motivated by financial gain or political ideologies. Opportunistic attackers.

21. Hacktivists
Individuals or groups that use their technical skills to promote a cause or drive social change instead of for personal gain

Website defacement, DDOS, Doxxing, Mass publishing of private data
Tend to have a fairly high level of sophistication, since their targets are specific

22. Organized Crime
Sophisticated and well structured entities that leverage resources and technical skills for illicit gain   $

Typically trans-national groups.

Causes issues and makes it harder once their trail leaves your nation’s borders


Highly adaptive like historical organized crime. It’s an arms race against consequences.

Commit crime, security tightens, figure out new method


Uses Cryto, Cellular Connection Devices, and Dark Web to obfuscate
Can be hired by other governments or organizations/groups

23. Nation-State Actors
Groups that are sponsored by a government to conduct cyber operations against other nations, organizations, or individuals.

False Flag Attack

Attack that is orchestrated in a way that it appears to originate from a different source/group

America has done these like daily in the middle east for going on 30-some-odd-years


Mimicking other nation’s methods or even code


Advanced persistent Threat

prolonged and targeted cyber attack. Monitoring for months/years


Typically nation state actors are motivated by long-term goals. If they take down a facility, what benefit do they get by taking it down? What larger goal might they have in mind?

Unless you’re broke like North Korea. They need money



24. Insider Threats
Threats that originate from within the organization. Abusing legitimate access

Outsider threats have no prior knowledge typically
Done for money, revenge, or carelessness

Untrained employees clicking links



25. Shadow IT
The use of information technology systems, devices, software, applications, and services without explicit organizational approval

Use of personal devices for work purposes
Installation of unapproved software

Plugins/Addons, too


Use of cloud services that have not been approved by the organization
Shadow IT exists typically because the security standards are too high and impede operations

Someone bringing in their own devices.



26. Threat Vectors and Attack Surfaces
Threat Vector (HOW)
The means or pathway by which an attacker can gain unauthorized access to a computer or network to deliver a malicious payload or carry out an unwanted action.

Messages

Phishing
Malicious links/files


Images

Imbedded malicious code inside of an image file

When the computer runs to display the image, the image can trigger something
Similar to uploading a reverse shell, then nagivaging to the webpage

IE: target.com/uploads/malicious-file-entity.php






Files
Voice Calls

Vishing ; Trick caller to give out info


Removable devices

USB thumb drives, External HDD


Unsecure Networks

Wifi, Bluetooth, wireless netoworks
Fake Access points




Attack Surface (WHERE)
Encompasses all the various points where an unauthorized user can try to enter data to or extract data from an environment.

Break down network into smaller parts to better analyze the attack surface.
Minimizing attack surface:

Restrict Access
Remove Unnecessary Software
Disabling Unused Protocols/Ports



27. Outsmarting Threat Actors
Be proactive! Not reactive!
Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTPs)
Specific methods and patterns of activities or behaviors associated with a particular threat actor or group of threat actors
Deceptive and Disruption Tech
Designed to mislead, confuse, and divert attackers from critical assets while simultaneously detecting and neutralizing threats

Honeypots

To install these in an enterprise network, place it within a screened subnet or isolated segment that is easily accessed by potential attackers


Honeynet

Network of honeypots to create a more complex system that is designed to mimic an entire network of systems including servers, routers, and switches
Logs all activities
Both Honeypots and Honeynets can be used by threat actors to learn more about the organization and how things are configured


Honeyfile

Decoy file placed within a system to lure in potential attackers
Once file is accessed, alert!
Sometimes honeyfiles are viruses in it of themselves
Can be any type of file. Images to documents or even executables.


Honeytoken - Study these more!!!

Piece of data or resource that has zero legitimate value/use, but is monitored for access or usage
Useful for detecting insider threats
fake admin login
Slowdown attackers on the main system:


Using bogus DNS entries
Creating decoy directories
Generating dynamic pages

Makes it harder for bots or scripts to enumerate


Port triggering

Security mechanism where specific services or ports on a network device remain closed until a specific outbound traffic pattern is detacted. Opening and closing the gates as needed


Spoofing fake telemetry data

Telemetry data is identifying info on a device. Windows/Macos, What web browser, system specs, etc.
Confuse attackers into believing a windows PC is linux or vice versa



Section 4: Physical Security
OBJ 1.2 + 2.4
Measures taken to protect tangible assets like buildings, equipment, and people from harm or other unauthorized access

Fences and Bollards

Fences are structures that encloses an area ; PREVENTS PEOPLE

Visual deterrent ; Shows clear barrier against unauthorized entry
Delays intruders ; Adds time to climb or dig your way around
Scale your walls to your needs. Big, tall and spiky or cute, painted, and short.


Bollards are robust, short, vertical posts that are made of steel in concrete that’s designed to manage or redirect vehicular traffic ; PREVENTS VEHICLES

Prevents vehicles to ram through/enter ; Mainly to protect pedestrians, but also to keep vehicle bombs outside of reach and to paint a clear barrier against vehicle traffic
Can artsy it up to make them more appealing ; Target red balls, Cement Planters
Not invulnerable ; There are bollard ratings ; Some bollards are removable




Attacking with Brute Force

Brute force is an attack where you try all of the possibilities to gain entry.
Physical brute force tactics include Forcible entry, Tampering with security devices, confronting security personnel, or ramming a barrier with a vehicle


Surveillance systems

Is an organized strategy or setup designed to observe and report activities in a given area
Include Video surveillance, security guards, lighting, and sensors

Indoor vs Outdoor equipment
Sensors include Infrared, Pressure, Microwave, and Ultrasonic

Microwave sensors detect movement






Bypassing Surveillance Systems

Include Visual Obstruction, Blinding sensors and cameras, Acoustic interference, Electromagnetic interference, and physical environment attack

Acoustic interference involves jamming or playing loud sounds to disrupt a microphone
EMI or Electromagnetic interference involves jamming signals that surveillance systems rely on to monitor


Prevent bypass implementing: Tamper alarms, backup power supply or UPS, encrypting frequencies


Access Control Vestibules

Electronically controlled double door system. One door can be open at a time ; very secure
Piggybacking & Tailgating are big issues

Tailgating is opportunistic, Piggybacking is consentual




Door Locks

Padlocks, pin and tumbler, numeric, wireless, biometric, cipher(PIN pad), electronic access control systems
Biometrics

Challenges include: False Acceptance Rate (FAR) , False Rejection Rate (FRR)
Good balance of FRR and FAR is the Equal Error Rate (EER) or more commonly Crossover Error Rate (CER)
Biometrics + PIN = epic offline 2FA (Both Biometrics and PIN needs to be correct before authentication. No Biometric success then PIN success)




Access badge controls

Card types

RFID
NFC


Security auditing ; Log every key usage



Definitions

Piggybacking

One person giving access to another in an area


Tailgating

Unauthorized person closely following without the other’s knowledge or consent



Section 5: Social Engineering
The backbone of social engineering lies in the ability of an attacker to trick a user into doing something for them
Objectives 2.2 & 5.6

Motivational Triggers (OBJ 5.6)
3. Authority
- Most people are willing to comply with authority
4. Urgency
- Causes people to act swiftly and not think critically
5. Social Proof
- People look to the behaviors and actions of others to gauge their own decisions or actions in a similar situation
- Likes, Shares, general approval online and offline ; Online Marketing LOL
6. Scarcity
- Causes Psychological pressure. Only while supply last!
7. Likability
- Friendly and attractive ;)
- Sexual attraction
- Hot women are skeleton keys to an IT team
- Pretending to be a friend
- Common interest
8. Fear
- Ape brain go brr when scared
Impersonation (OBJ 2.2)

Impersonation

Pretend to be someone that’s liked, trusted, or a figure of authority


Brand Impersonation

Like the danimals zach and cody sweepstakes, but by some random guy (It’s a scam either way)


Typo-Squatting

Registers a domain that is similar to a popular website. Remember the old scam CSGO trade websites? THAT is typo-squatting


Watering Hole Attacks

Compromise a specific website or service that their target(s) is/are known to use.
Somebody poisoned the water hole!




Pretexting (OBJ 2.2)

Create a convincing message or fabricated story to send, a Pre-text!

Impersonate a trusted figure or authority figure
Use the story to use as a crowbar to wedge more questions in




Phishing Attacks (OBJ 2.2)

Phishing

Fraudulent emails from a trusted source to trick people into disclosing personal or private information
Wide net attack, typically many targets


Spear Phishing

Like Phishing, but targeted on a specific group of people or organizations
More targeted with a higher success rate


Whaling

Form of Spear Phishing that targets high-profile individuals like CEOs, Execs, or CFOs


Business Email Compromise

Uses a compromised business email to send seemingly legitimate requests


Vishing

Voice Phishing ; Phone-based attack


Smshing

Text messages Phishing




Preventing Phishing Attacks (OBJ 5.6)

Anti-phishing Campaigns/trainings

Regularly provide user security awareness training that covers various phishing techniques
In-depth remedial training from failing simulated phishing attack


Hover cursor on link to verify URL. You can spoof a legit link by using a hyperlink
Spot poor grammar and spelling
Report suspicious messages
Inform all users about the threat


Conducting an Anti-Phishing Campaign (OBJ 5.6)

Simulate a phishing attack ; Phish insight
Phishing insight has all sorts of crazy phishing testing with automated emailing


Frauds and Scams (OBJ 2.2)

Identity Fraud/Theft

Fraud uses the victim’s credit card and makes charges
Theft is fully assuming the identity of their victim


Scams

Invoice Scam

Tricked into paying a fake invoice for a service or product they did not order
Can send an infected PDF invoice for further damage; Can install a RAT






Influence Campaigns (OBJ 2.2)

Is a powerful tool for shaping public opinion and behavior ; Misinformation is commonly used


Other Social Engineering Attacks (OBJ 2.2)

Diversion Theft

Manipulating a situation or causing a distraction to steal valuable items or information


Hoaxes

Malicious deception that is often spread through social media, email, or other coms


Shoulder Surfing

Looking over someone’s shoulder, at a desk, phone, or terminal, to gather personal information
Modern tech  like cameras, or cctv make this easier


Dumpster Diving
Eavesdropping
Baiting

Planting an infected device for a victim to find and unintentionally introduce malware to the org ; Dumping USBs in a parking lot


Piggybacking
Tailgating



Definitions
Social Engineering is a manipulative strategy that exploits human psychology to gain unauthorized access to systems, data, information/knowledge, or physical spaces
Misinformation is inaccurate information shared unintentionally
Disinformation is the intentional spread of false information to deceive or mislead
Section 6: Malware
Objective 2.4

Viruses

Boot Sector Viruses are stored in the boot partition of your disk and start on bootup and typical AVs struggle with detecting these. Need a boot partition antivirus
Macro Viruses are typically embedded in files that can execute macros
Program viruses try to find application files to infect with malicious code
Multipartite Viruses are a combination of a boot sector and program viruses. Hide on boot, install after boot
Encrypted viruses evade antivirus detection by using encryption
Polymorphic viruses are more advanced than encrypted viruses. The code is changed each time it’s executed by altering the decryption module
Metamorphic viruses are even more advanced than polymorphic. They’re able to rewrite itself entirely before it attempts to infect a given file
Stealth viruses refer to a type of technique. Think any virus that tries to hide itself from the AV
Armored viruses have a layer of protection to confuse a program or person who’s trying to analyze it
Hoax is a form of technical social engineering that attempts to scare end users into taking undesirable actions on their system. Think !!!ALERT YOU WON A FREE IPHONE!!! type websites


Worms

Worms operate all on their own and will spread across the network
They can cause disruptions to the normal network traffic since they are constantly trying to spread through the network


Trojans

Remote Access Trojan (RAT) ; Provides attacker with remote control of target device


Ransomware

REGULARLY BACKUP PLEASE OMFG
NEVER pay the ransom ; Paying doesn’t guarantee your data
Once infected, disconnect from the network


Zombies and Botnets

Many zombies in a botnet
Command and Control Node (C2 node): Responsible for managing and coordinating the activities of other nodes or devices within a network


Rootkits

Designed to dig deep into the OS

DLL Injections are used to run code within the address space of another process
Shims are software code that intercepts OS “calls”




Backdoors and Logic Bombs

Backdoors are terrible security design

RATs are a type of backdoor


Easter eggs are bad security practice as they add unnecessary attack surface
Logic bombs are glyphs of warding. If specific thing happens, then do this

Check Active Directory nightly. If I get fired turn everything off




Keylogger

Hardware keyloggers are harder to detect than software ones
Always visually check for hardware loggers


Spyware and Bloatware

Bloatware adds attack surface


Malware Attack Techniques

Fileless malware hard to detect
Malware is usually multi-staged with each stage or malware having it’s own specific purpose. One infects, the next one downloads extra stuff, final one does something, etc.
Malware hiding techniques

Code injection, Masquerading, DLL injection, DLL sideloading, process hollowing




Indications of Malware Attacks

Common indicators

Account Lockouts
Blocked Content reports (In orgs, mainly
)
Resource consumption
Out-of-cycle logging
published or documented attacks
Concurrent session utilization
Impossible travel
Resource inaccessibility
Missing Logs





Definitions
Malware is any software that is designed to infiltrate a computer system without the user’s knowledge
Threat Vector is a potential method used by an attacker to infiltrate a victim’s machine ; How someone could break in ; Theoretical
Attack Vector is the means by which an attacker gains access to a computer to infect the system with malware ; How someone broke in and infected the device ; Real-life scenario
Virus is malicious software that attaches to clean files and spreads into a computer system
Worms are standalone malware programs that replicate and spread to other systems by exploiting software vulnerabilities
Trojans are malicious programs which appear to be legitimate software that allow unauthorized access to a victim’s system when executed
Ransomware encrypts a user’s data and holds it hostage until a ransom is paid to the attacker for decryption
Zombies are compromised computers that are remotely controlled by attackers and used in coordination to form a botnet
Botnet is a network of zombies and are often used for DDoS attacks, spam distribution, or cryptocurrency mining
Rootkits are malicious tools that hide their activities and operate at the OS level to allow for top level privileged access
Backdoors are malicious means of bypassing normal authentication process to gain unauthorized access to a system
Logic Bombs are embedded code placed in legitimate programs that executes a malicious action when a specific condition or trigger occurs.
Keyloggers record a user’s keystrokes and are used to capture passwords or other sensitive information
Spyware secretly monitors and gather’s user information or activities and sends the data to a third party.
Bloatware is unnecessary or pre-installed software that consumes system resources and space without offering any value to the user
Malware Exploitation Techniques Involve methods by which malware infiltrates and infects targeted systems
Fileless Malware Used to create a process in the system memory without relying on the local file system of the infected host
Dropper initiates or runs other malware forms within a payload on an infected host
Downloaders retrieves additional tools post the initial infection facilitated by a dropper
Shellcode Encompasses lightweight code meant to execute an exploit on a given target
Section 7: Data Protection
OBJ 1.4, 3.3, 4.2, 4.4, 5.1

Data Classifications (OBJ 3.3)

Over classifying data leads to protecting all data at a high level ; Requires too much resources for something like a water bill
Commercial Business Scheme

Public - No impact on the company if released
Sensitive - Minimal impact ; financial data
Private - Data that should only be used within the org ; employee HR data, internal revenue
Confidential - Contains items such as trade secrets, intellectual properties, and source code ; Like comptia’s test questions
Critical - Valuable information like credit cards


Government Classifications

Unclassified - Data that can be released to the public or under Freedom of Information Act
Sensitive but unclassified - Data that would not harm national security, but could impact those whose data was being used ; internal Medical records and personal files
Confidential - Data that could seriously affect the government ; Trade secrets
Secret - Data that could seriously damage national security ; military =plans=/defensive postures
Top Secret - will damage national security if disclosed


Data should not be stored forever

Collect > Retain > Dispose




Data Ownership (OBJ 4.2) (OBJ 5.1) REVIEW

The creator of data may not always be the owner
Data owners should not be IT, but someone related to the data itself. Accountants own accounting, HR owns employee records
Data roles

Owners are responsible for maintaining the CIA triad of the information
Controllers decides the purposes and methods of data storage, collection, usage, and for guaranteeing the legality
Processor is a group or individual hired by the controller to help with tasks like collecting, storing, or analyzing data
Custodian are responsible for handling the management of the system where the data is stored ; Sysadmins
Steward are focused on the quality of the data and it’s associated metadata
Privacy Officer oversight of any privacy-related data like PII, SPI, or PHI




Data States (OBJ 3.3)

Data at Rest is any data stored in databases, file systems, or other storage systems. PRIME TARGET FOR ATTACKERS

Defend with: Full Disk Encryption, Partition Encryption, File Encryption, Volume Encryption, Database Encryption, and Record Encryption

Volume encryption is encrypting a set of files/directories




Data in Transit/Data in Motion is any data actively moving from one location to another. From server to server, or copying a file on the local system to another area

Defend with SSL/TLS, VPNs, and IPSec


Data in use is any bit of data being used

Encrypt data at the application level,
Implement access controls, secure enclaves
Intel software guard can encrypt data in memory

Security Program Management and Oversight

SLA (Service-Level Agreement) – Defines service expectations (uptime, support, performance).
MOA (Memorandum of Agreement) – Formal document outlining agreed responsibilities between parties.
MOU (Memorandum of Understanding) – Less formal than MOA, expresses intent to cooperate.
MSA (Master Service Agreement) – Governs future work; sets standard terms for multiple projects.
WO (Work Order) – Authorization to perform specific tasks or services.
SOW (Statement of Work) – Details the scope, deliverables, and timeline of a project.
NDA (Non-Disclosure Agreement) – Legally prevents sharing confidential information.
BPA (Business Partners Agreement) – Defines roles, responsibilities, and expectations between partners.
AUP (Acceptable Use Policy) – Defines proper and improper use of company resources.
SDLC (Software Development Lifecycle) – Framework for developing software securely and systematically.
BIA (Business Impact Analysis) – Identifies critical systems and the effect of disruptions.
GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) – EU regulation for protecting personal data and privacy.
PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard) – Rules for securing credit/debit card transactions.
ISO (International Organization for Standardization) – Develops global standards, including security (e.g., ISO 27001).
CSA (Cloud Security Alliance) – Provides best practices and security guidance for cloud computing.
IRP (Incident Response Plan) – Steps to detect, respond to, and recover from incidents.
IoC (Indicators of Compromise) – Signs that a system or network may have been breached.
BCP (Business Continuity Plan) – Ensures business functions can continue during/after a disruption.
COOP (Continuity of Operations Plan) – Federal/government-focused plan for essential operations.
DRP (Disaster Recovery Plan) – Procedures to restore IT systems and data after a disaster.
RTO (Recovery Time Objective) – Maximum downtime acceptable before systems must be restored.
RPO (Recovery Point Objective) – Maximum data loss acceptable, measured in time (e.g., last 4 hours of work).
AV (Asset Value) – Monetary worth of an asset.
EF (Exposure Factor) – Percentage of asset lost if a risk occurs.
SLE (Single Loss Expectancy) – Expected monetary loss from one incident (AV × EF).
ARO (Annualized Rate of Occurrence) – How often a risk is expected to occur in a year. This is bolt
ALE (Annualized Loss Expectancy) – Yearly expected loss (SLE × ARO).
MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures) – Average time between system failures (repairable systems).
MTTF (Mean Time to Failure) – Average lifespan before a system fails (non-repairable).
MTTR (Mean Time to Repair) – Average time to fix a failed system and restore service.

Security Operations

MDM (Mobile Device Management) – Centralized control of mobile devices for security and compliance.
BYOD (Bring Your Own Device) – Policy allowing employees to use personal devices for work.
COPE (Corporate-Owned, Personally Enabled) – Company provides devices but allows limited personal use.
CYOD (Choose Your Own Device) – Employees choose from a list of approved company devices.
WPA3 (Wi-Fi Protected Access 3) – Latest Wi-Fi security standard with stronger encryption and protection.
RADIUS (Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service) – Centralized authentication, authorization, and accounting protocol.
Application Security – Practices and controls to protect software during development and use.
Input Validation – Checking user data to ensure it meets expected format and prevents malicious input.
Secure Cookies – Cookies flagged to only transmit over HTTPS connections.
Static Code Analysis – Reviewing source code without running it to find vulnerabilities or errors.
Code Signing – Digitally verifying software’s source and integrity.
Sandboxing – Running code in isolation to prevent it from affecting the main system.

Security Architecture
IPS (Intrusion Prevention System) – Monitors and blocks malicious traffic in real time.
IDS (Intrusion Detection System) – Detects and alerts on suspicious or malicious activity.
EAP (Extensible Authentication Protocol) – Authentication framework commonly used in wireless networks.
WAF (Web Application Firewall) – Protects web apps by filtering and monitoring HTTP/HTTPS traffic.
UTM (Unified Threat Management) – All-in-one security solution combining multiple functions (firewall, IDS/IPS, AV, etc.).
NGFW (Next-Generation Firewall) – Firewall with advanced features like deep packet inspection and application control.
IaC (Infrastructure as Code) – Managing infrastructure with machine-readable configuration files.

Microservices – Application architecture of small, independent services working together.

Passive Device – Device that only observes traffic.

Responsibility Matrix (RACI) – Defines who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed.
IoT (Internet of Things) – Network of connected devices that collect and exchange data.
Embedded Systems – Specialized computers built into larger systems for specific tasks.
Remote Access – Ability to connect to systems/networks from outside locations.
Tunneling – Encapsulating one data packet inside another for secure transfer.
VPN (Virtual Private Network) – Encrypted tunnel providing secure remote access.
TLS (Transport Layer Security) – Protocol securing communications over the internet.
IPSec (Internet Protocol Security) – Suite of protocols securing IP traffic via encryption and authentication.
SD-WAN (Software-Defined Wide Area Network) – WAN managed through software for flexible routing.
SASE (Secure Access Service Edge) – Cloud framework combining networking and security services.
Data at Rest – Stored data on disks or other storage.
Data in Use/Processing – Data actively being processed in RAM.
Data in Transit/Motion – Data moving across networks.
Data Sovereignty – Legal principle that data is subject to laws of the country where it resides.
Geolocation – Identifying the physical location of a device or user.
High Availability – System designed to remain operational with minimal downtime.
Load Balancing – Distributing traffic across multiple servers to prevent overload.
Clustering – Linking servers together to work as one system for redundancy/performance.
Snapshots – Point-in-time backups of systems or data.
Cold Site – Backup facility with basic infrastructure, no equipment installed.
Warm Site – Backup site with hardware available but data must be restored.
Hot Site – Fully equipped backup site with real-time mirrored data.
COOP (Continuity of Operations Plan) – Ensures essential functions continue during/after disruption.
UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) – Backup power device that keeps systems running during outages.

Statement of Work (SOW) - This agreement outlines the specific services to be provided by the vendor, along with associated timelines and costs

Masking - Is a technique that replaces sensitive data with fictitious, but structurally similar, data.

Role-Based Access Control - Within Zero trust, Role Based Access Control permissions are assigned based on predefined roles in an organization, and individuals are then assigned to those roles.

Digital Signatures

Digital signatures are used to verify what was sent is not only accurate, but sent from the expected person
To create one, you take the sent data and hash it. From there, you use your private key to encrypt the hash for transit.
To verify a signature, you hash the received data, then you decrypt the signature with the sender’s public key to receive a hash, then finally you compare the two hashes.


Key Stretching

Key stretching is the act of applying a hashing algorithm multiple times to make it much harder to crack (computationally speaking)


Blockchain

the blockchain is an open ledger that is hosted all across the internet. This ledger tracks and records all activities happening. Most typical uses of a blockchain are for cryptocurrencies and NFTs


Open Public Ledger

The broader umbrella term for things like blockchains


Certificates

Certificates are typically created from trusted sources, Certificate authorities, that are used to create trust. If you trust the CA, you trust the certificate
Certficate Authorities - Are the generally trusted vendors that give out certificates to online services. Their business model is being trusted to verify online services/websites so that bad actors have a harder time tricking others.
Certificate Revocation Lists - List of certificates that lose validity before their expected expiration date
Online Certificate status Protocol (OCSP)
Self-Signed - Certificates can be signed by yourself, but that doesn’t immediately mean that it’s something to be trusted.
Third-Party - The usual defacto way to get your websites and other online services verified. These third parties are generally trusted to verify who you say you are
Root of trust - the highest level of trust in a certificate. Could be you if you self-sign, could be a certificate authority otherwise.
Certificate Signing Request (CSR) generation - A request sent to a certificate authority to receive a certificate
Wildcard - Blanket certificate for subdomains
